study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within a registry-linked cohort, using incidence-density sampled controls
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Complete data for all investigated exposures was available for 483 eligible cases and 1055 eligible controls.
reason: The study evaluated incident overall prostate cancer among initially healthy men but did not report an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Background To evaluate the individual and combined effects of enterolactone, vitamin D, free testosterone, Chlamydia trachomatis and HPV-18 on the risk of prostate cancer in a large population-based biochemical material that combined three Nordic serum sample banks.
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin D analysis concerns overall incident prostate cancer, with no aggressive endpoint established.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
